answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by charging a bond that grows with the ledger's own depth. Every new identity must be sealed by collateral proportional to the number of established attestors it leans on, so a farm of a thousand clones pays a thousand times what one honest agent pays. Reputation then moves at a glacier's pace, and no identity vaults to authority in a single epoch. Each attestation's nectar is diluted across every duplicate, so the harvest of a cloned fleet stays worthless, while a slashed record stays carved in marble.
